competing_implementations: apply lane tip commit only: git cherry-pick <lane_tip>
apply full lane commit range: git cherry-pick <lane_merge_base>..<lane_tip>
decisions.contract: Every file in git diff --name-only <merge_base>..<lane_tip> must exist in git ls-files after integration.
decisions.rationale: Tip-only application silently dropped lane work: RQ4 (2 commits) and RQ5 (23 commits) lost commits, leaving 11 of 13 RQ4 files absent (including ultimate_pipeline/domain_gap_gnn/reproducibility_pack.py) while the cherry-pick reported success. Detected by re-verifying every lane file against git ls-files after integration. Remediated by git reset --hard to the pre-lane commit and re-applying all three lanes as explicit ranges.
decisions.regression_test: tools/integration_lineage_audit.py lane file-presence verification; ALL_LANE_FILES_PRESENT=True recorded in INTEGRATION_COMPLETENESS.json
decisions.selected_behavior: Apply the full range <merge_base>..<lane_tip> for every lane.

competing_implementations: empty commit in the RQ5 range (no tree change)
decisions.contract: No content loss; verified by full lane file presence check.
decisions.rationale: The commit had an empty tree diff, so it carried no content. Skipping preserves history order without introducing an empty commit.
